subject: Vendor access: split identity prevents PO generation - urgent
messages:
From: Kevin Liu <kevin@harborforge.co>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Trouble accepting PO - two supplier records in Coupa

Rafael,

We're blocked from accepting the PO you raised yesterday. When Accounts Payable tries to view the PO in Coupa it shows a different vendor record and the 'Accept' button is disabled. Our side shows two supplier entries for Harbor Forge — one tied to our legacy vendor account (legacy@harborforge.co) and one tied to our new procurement domain (ap@harborforge.co).

I attached a quick screenshot (screenshot_coupa_error.png) showing the error that reads: "Supplier record mismatch: vendor must be single identity to accept PO." Our finance team is asking for either: (a) a merged supplier profile on your side, or (b) a manual PO we can acknowledge while you work the merge.

Can you advise the fastest route? This PO is time-sensitive — we have shipments scheduled and a supplier hold will push our deliveries.

Thanks,
Kevin Liu
Head of Supply Chain
Harbor Forge

Attachment: screenshot_coupa_error.png

From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
To: Kevin Liu <kevin@harborforge.co>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Trouble accepting PO - two supplier records in Coupa

Kevin — thanks for flagging this and for the screenshot. Sorry for the disruption.

Short answer: we can do a quick manual workaround (issue a temporary PO to the legacy supplier record) while procurement and supplier ops merge the two Coupa profiles. Long answer: looks like our onboarding sync created a duplicate when Harbor Forge updated their remit email; the supplier id linked to the new domain didn't pick up the legacy vendor attributes used for PO acceptance.

I've looped in Ben (supplier ops) and Marissa (procurement) to own the merge and the PO routing. For now, can you confirm whether Harbor Forge's finance team can receive POs at legacy@harborforge.co for an interim 48–72 hour window? If yes, we'll reissue a PO to that remit address and mark it as temporary. Also attaching your vendor spreadsheet I requested — if you can confirm bank remit and TAX ID I will push it into our supplier portal.

Rafael
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: harbor_vendor_profile.xlsx

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Kevin Liu <kevin@harborforge.co>
Date: 2026-11-02T08:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Trouble accepting PO - two supplier records in Coupa

Rafael / Marissa — dug into the supplier snapshot. Coupa shows two supplier records: SupplierID 908712 (legacy@harborforge.co) and SupplierID 981204 (ap@harborforge.co). The records have different remit_to and tax profiles; our auto-mapping created the second on a domain change and didn't merge on vendor_name matching because there was a small legal-name punctuation difference.

Technical options (ranked by speed):
1) Temporary PO: Procurement reissue PO to SupplierID 908712 (legacy) and flag "manual remit override" in the PO notes — Kevin's AP can acknowledge and process. I can toggle the PO route within 2 hours.
2) Merge supplier records in Coupa: requires Supplier Ops to request an admin merge with Coupa support; ETA 24–48 hours depending on support lane. We'll need Harbor Forge to confirm the canonical TAX ID and bank remit.
3) Create a new remit alias routing rule in our gateway so both supplier IDs route to the same account — more involved, ETA 3–5 business days.

I'll prepare the snapshot and the minimal instructions to reissue the temporary PO. Attaching a small export for reference (coupa_supplier_snapshot.json).

Ben Carter
Supplier Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: coupa_supplier_snapshot.json

From: Kevin Liu <kevin@harborforge.co>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai, accounts-payable@harborforge.co
Date: 2026-11-02T10:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Trouble accepting PO - two supplier records in Coupa

Marissa / Ben — thanks for the quick responses. Harbor Forge can accept an interim PO at legacy@harborforge.co for 72 hours. Confirming our canonical TAX ID is 12-3456789 and the remit bank is HarborForge Banking (routing instructions in the attached vendor profile).

We'd prefer you do the merge in Coupa so future POs route cleanly, but interim PO is fine. Please send the temporary PO number once it's reissued and we'll acknowledge immediately. Also please include a short mutual action plan (who will submit the merge request, what support docs you need) so I can escalate internally.

Kevin

From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
To: Kevin Liu <kevin@harborforge.co>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-03T15:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Trouble accepting PO - two supplier records in Coupa

Kevin — agreed. We will: 
- Reissue PO temporarily to SupplierID 908712 (legacy) within the hour and deliver PO_2026-11-03_TEMP908712 to your AP (accounts-payable@harborforge.co).
- Marissa will open the Coupa merge ticket with our supplier operations team and request admin merge; Ben will prepare the support payload (TAX ID, bank remit proof). Target ETA: 24–48 hours. Ticket: SUP-3421 (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-3421).
- Kimberly will validate the routing rule post-merge and confirm no downstream PO automation is impacted.

I'll follow up once the temporary PO is sent. If Harbor Forge can sign and ack within 24 hours it will avoid shipment delay.

Thanks for moving quickly on this.

Rafael Mendes
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: po_temp_workaround_instructions.pdf
